tests.title: BatchWriter (real Postgres) inserts 100 rows in one statement
BatchWriter (real Postgres) [G2.same-chunk-twice] writing the same chunk again inserts 0, reports every key as a duplicate, table unchanged
BatchWriter (real Postgres) a duplicate inside one chunk is absorbed in the same statement (DO NOTHING, not DO UPDATE)
BatchWriter (real Postgres) [G2.tenant-scope] the same event_id under two tenants is stored twice
BatchWriter (real Postgres) [G2.conflict] same key, different content: first stored copy wins, the conflict is reported
BatchWriter (real Postgres) a duplicate with the same content in another form (key order, offset time zone) is NOT a conflict
BatchWriter (real Postgres) stores received_at from the header, payload as jsonb, content_hash, and stored_at after received_at
BatchWriter (real Postgres) a failing chunk leaves nothing behind (transaction rolled back)
BatchWriter (real Postgres) sink_offsets (same transaction as the rows) records the highest offset per partition and never moves it back (GREATEST)
BatchWriter (real Postgres) sink_offsets (same transaction as the rows) is rolled back together with the rows when the chunk fails
BatchWriter (real Postgres) sink_offsets (same transaction as the rows) is advanced even when every row was a duplicate (the offset WAS processed)
S2-F3 commit protocol (real process) crash after the DB commit, before the offset commit: no loss, duplicates bounded by one chunk
S2-F3 commit protocol (real process) crash at before_parse: no loss and no duplicate rows
S2-F3 commit protocol (real process) crash at after_parse: no loss and no duplicate rows
S2-F3 commit protocol (real process) committed offset = last processed offset + 1 (the next offset to read), exactly at the log end
S2-F3 commit protocol (real process) database unreachable: no offset advances while it is down; after it returns every row is stored
S2-F3 commit protocol (real process) SIGTERM under load: the current chunk finishes and commits, nothing is lost, nothing replayed
pipeline (real processes) POST 1000 events to the real API: all 1000 rows in Postgres within a bounded delay
pipeline (real processes) 3 members on a 2-partition topic: exactly 2 get a partition, the third is idle, and delivery works
pipeline (real processes) S2-F6 consumer metrics after a run: lag 0, inserted = new rows, freshness samples; a 2nd member -> rebalances
S2-F4 poison messages (real process) invalid-json in the middle of a busy partition: the partition drains, the record is in the DLQ
S2-F4 poison messages (real process) bad-uuid in the middle of a busy partition: the partition drains, the record is in the DLQ
S2-F4 poison messages (real process) oversized-field in the middle of a busy partition: the partition drains, the record is in the DLQ
S2-F4 poison messages (real process) constraint in the middle of a busy partition: the partition drains, the record is in the DLQ
S2-F4 poison messages (real process) Postgres unreachable for 20 s under load: zero records dead-lettered, everything stored after recovery
S2-F4 poison messages (real process) Postgres container STOPPED for 30 s under load (plan 4.4): zero dead letters, all rows after restart
S2-F4 poison messages (real process) SINK_DLQ_ENABLED=false reproduces the blocking: the poison partition stops, the others drain
consumer-sink: Kafka -> Postgres writes 1000 events (all 6 partitions) to Postgres within a bounded delay
consumer-sink: Kafka -> Postgres duplicate records: one row each, and the duplicates are counted
consumer-sink: Kafka -> Postgres a second member splits the partitions: none owned twice, all six owned
consumer-sink: Kafka -> Postgres restart resumes from committed offsets: events produced while down are written, nothing replayed
